title: demolish_button_rect keeps an unscaled nil-default twin; parity harness already calls the unscaled branch
detail: Two hand-synced copies of the button rect (scaled + raw). A caller omitting the view — as parity.odin:976 does — silently gets unscaled geometry, diverging from the drawn (scaled) button at ×1.25/×1.50. This is the codebase's named debt class.
recommended_fix: Delete the nil-default branch; make `v: ^View` required. Update harness/parity.odin:976 to pass the in-scope `view`, matching demolish_btn_center at parity.odin:964.

title: pulse_read 'ONE seam' claim is false — crisis outline inlines its own reduced-motion gate over raw PULSE16
evidence: view.odin:352: "// 7.3 (E9.2): the motion-gated pulse read — the ONE seam every animated / pulse consumer routes through."  ---  crisis.odin:174-182: "// static at full width (pulse_read) — the banner + glyph + the outline / // itself still carry the crisis (the readability contract). / table := PULSE16 / phase := (tick + u64(b)) % 16 / factor := table[phase] / if v.reduced_motion { / factor = 1.0 / }"
detail: The reduced-motion gate now exists at two sites that must be hand-synced. The crisis comment even cites pulse_read while the code bypasses it, so a future motion-rule change (e.g. pin value) diverges ring vs outline.
recommended_fix: Extract a shared gate (e.g. motion_pin(v, factor) -> f32 returning 1.0 under reduced_motion) in view.odin; route both draw_health_ring and draw_crisis_outlines through it, keeping each site's own phase math.

title: settings_click is duplicated as a hand-synced parity twin instead of one shared input-package proc
evidence: parity.odin:135-139: "// parity_settings_press_effect — the settings chip/row press (7.3), the parity / twin of the app's settings_click: mirrors the INPUT-STATE mutations (panel / open/close + focus + the row-adjust)..."  ---  main.odin:795-798: "if rl.CheckCollisionPointRec(pos, rnd.settings_chip_rect(&app.view)) { / app.input.panel_open = false / effect_settings(app.input.user, &app.input)"  ---  main.odin convention: "// the body lives in the input package (right_click_select) — ONE copy, / shared with the harness parity hook (Perkins note: no drift)"
detail: The codebase's stated convention for app+parity hit logic is ONE shared copy in the input package (popover_demolish_hit, right_click_select). The settings surface instead ships two copies that must be edited in lockstep; the on_settings/on_settings_adjust hooks already enable a single copy.
recommended_fix: Move settings_click's input-state mutations into app/input (e.g. settings_press(inp, pos) -> bool invoking the hooks); the app and parity both wire it, deleting parity_settings_press_effect's hand-mirrored copy.

title: a11y state triple-mirrored (App.a11y, view.reduced_motion/ui_scale, palette.mode) and hand-synced at two sites
evidence: main.odin:766-768: "case rnd.SETTINGS_ROW_MOTION: / app.a11y.reduced_motion = !app.a11y.reduced_motion / app.view.reduced_motion = app.a11y.reduced_motion"  ---  main.odin:1253-1258: "snap := rnd.Settings_Snapshot{ / mode = app.a11y.palette, / reduced_motion = app.view.reduced_motion, / ui_scale = app.view.ui_scale, / muted = au.is_muted(&app.audio), / }"  ---  settings_panel.odin: "scaled := v.ui_scale > 1.001 || v.palette.mode != .Off || v.reduced_motion"
detail: The chip reads palette.mode while the panel snapshot reads app.a11y.palette/view fields — same fact, two sources, synced only by init + effect_settings_adjust. A future writer touching one mirror desyncs chip, panel, or persistence.
recommended_fix: Pick one source per fact (e.g. snapshot mode from app.palette.mode; derive scale_step at save time via step_of), or add a single apply_a11y(app) proc that owns all mirror writes.

title: ui_scale zero-guard lives only in view_compute; hud()/hud_f() silently collapse on a view that skips it
evidence: view.odin:104-107: "// 7.3: the UI-scale default — every View starts at ×1.00 (a zero-inited / View would make hud() return 0). The app/harness override per settings. / if v.ui_scale <= 0 { / v.ui_scale = 1.0 / }"  ---  view.odin:365-367: "hud :: proc(v: ^View, k: i32) -> i32 { / return i32(f32(k) * v.ui_scale + 0.5) / }"
detail: The ×1.00-identity invariant is enforced at the construction gate, not the read. Every current path calls view_compute (verified: app, parity, palcheck, goldens), but a future View constructed without it gets all-HUD-zero rects silently.
recommended_fix: Clamp inside the helpers (hud/hud_f return k when v.ui_scale <= 0), making the single-source read self-guarding; view_compute's guard can stay as documentation.
